title: Beanstalk: the next sum follows the child, not the calendar
wrong: The sum (10, 20, 100, 1000) is set by Golden Eggs, so a child who is not secure moves on after 30 days and a fast child waits. Pairs are one sum only and the weakest do not come up more.
done: A child stays on a sum until two good days and the facts are secure, steps back after two hard days, and gets about 2 older pairs in 10 with the weakest pairs most often.
why: Help and level follow the child, not the calendar; old facts are mixed in.

title: Beanstalk: missing-leaf goes are fair
wrong: On missing-leaf goes a wrong pair is blocked from a second try, and a go can float only two choices.
done: Missing-leaf goes always float at least 3 leaves, a wrong pair can be tried again, and the first one is shown with a pointing hand.
why: Guessing must not work, and a mistake should be free to retry; show the first time a new kind appears.

title: Teacher view catches up with the longer ladders
wrong: Hop steps 3, 4 and 200 and Penguin Pairs level 5 have no name in the teacher view, and 'top' is wrong for both.
done: Every reachable level has a name, 'top' is the real top, a test fails when a level is added without a name, and Beanstalk shows its sum.
why: The teacher needs honest, readable evidence of where each child is.

title: Same-day replays must not move the level
wrong: The level is worked out again on every finish, so a practice replay can push a child up or change tomorrow's round.
done: The level changes only at the day's first finish; replays still save answers but do not move the level.
why: Practice replays must not move the level.

title: Full help ends sooner for a child who already knows it
wrong: A fact keeps full help until it is right on two different days, and Tūī's level floor cancels the fade so a perfect child stays on level 4 for about 8 days.
done: Two quick rights, even on one day, end full help for that fact; a wrong answer brings it back; a perfect Tūī round starts the fade.
why: Help follows the child: fade on right-and-quick, return on struggle.

title: Penguin Pairs: the child shares the fish, and the near double is true
wrong: At full help the half goes share the fish by themselves, and the near-double picture draws its extra fish inside the reflection.
done: The child deals the fish at every help level, and the near double is a true mirror of n plus one separate fish.
why: The maths is the move, and pictures must be true.

title: Pipi: outlines do not give the answer, levels mix older sums, wrong shells tidy up
wrong: Full and faint help show one outline per hidden pipi, so counting outlines is the answer. Levels never revisit older sums. Wrong shells stay greyed in the row.
done: Outlines appear only after a first wrong try, about 2 goes in 10 are from earlier levels, and a wrong shell leaves once its reason is shown.
why: Help must not give the answer; mix old facts; mistakes teach then get out of the way.

title: Quick looks: hear the question, get a second try, drop the 4 second struggle rule
wrong: The question is read only if a child turns the voice on, a wrong answer shows the answer at once with no second try, and thinking over 4 seconds counts as struggling.
done: Young children hear the question by default, a wrong first answer brings the picture back for one more try, and only two wrong in a row count as struggling.
why: Voice first, mistakes teach, and fair timing.
